transcript.content:
<issue>
Flag mixing up "flaunt" and "flout"
**"Flaunt"** means to show off / be ostentatious. **"Flout"** means to openly ignore rules.

This doesn't seem to be common on GitHub but on the wider internet "flaunt" is a very common mistake where "flout" is obviously meant. (The reverse is nowhere near as common.)

- He **flaunted** US bankruptcy laws for personal gain.
- It's got a Kirk-esque captain who **flaunts** the rules in favour of 'getting her done' and who is fiercely loyal to his people.
- That's what deranged scientists **flaunting** the laws of God and Man are for
- While a lot of users have genuine trouble writing questions up in English, some seem to **flaunt** the basic rules of punctuation and grammar.

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, find how existing word-confusion rules are defined (e.g. grep for a similar rule like "affect"/"effect" or "loose"/"lose" in rule files, and how tests for them look). Report the file paths, and the exact contents of a short representative rule with its surrounding code (30 lines), and any list/registry where rules must be added.

{"summary":"Harper has two ways to define word-confusion rules. Short ones are declarative Weir `.weir` files in harper-core/src/linting/weir_rules/. These are auto-registered by build.rs, so no manual list edit is needed. Complex ones are Rust ExprLinters (e.g. all_hell_break_loose.rs). Those must be registered manually in mod.rs and lint_group.rs. Weir tests are inline in the `.weir` file. Rust tests live in a `#[cfg(test)]` module and use assert_suggestion_result. I did not run the build or tests.","findings":["Weir rules directory: harper-core/src/linting/weir_rules/ (248 files). A separate top-level /testbed/weir_rules/ has 37 files, e.g. ColdModalTypo.weir, and is not the dir build.rs reads. I did not find what uses it.","Registry for Weir: harper-core/build.rs:5-30 reads src/linting/weir_rules, sorts the `*.weir` files and generates weir_rules_generated_list.rs (`generate_boilerplate!{[...]}`). harper-core/src/linting/lint_group.rs:590 merges them with `out.merge_from(&mut weir_rules::lint_group())`. harper-core/src/linting/mod.rs:244 has `mod weir_rules;`. A new .weir file needs no other registration.","Representative short rule, harper-core/src/linting/weir_rules/ToLoseTooLoose.weir (whole file, 8 lines):
expr main [(to loose), (too lose)]

let message "For `not to win`, use `to lose`. For `not tight enough`, use `too loose`."
let description "Corrects mixing up `to` with `too` and `lose` with `loose`."
let kind "Spelling"
let becomes ["to lose", "too loose"]

test "...a pity to loose" "...a pity to lose"
test "...preconditions too lose and/or conflict..." "...preconditions too loose and/or conflict..."
(the two test lines are shortened here; the real file has full sentences)","Another short Weir rule, weir_rules/BadRap.weir: `expr main [(bed rap), (bad rep)]`, then let message, description, kind "Eggcorn", becomes "bad rap", then `test "bad rep" "bad rap"`.","Weir fields used: `expr main`, `let message/description/kind/becomes/strategy`, `test "bad" "good"`, and `allows "text"` for negatives. ColdModalTypo.weir shows `expr` sub-definitions with @refs and `let strategy "MatchCase"`. Weir docs: packages/web/src/routes/docs/weir/+page.md. AGENTS.md:118-143 has the Weir workflow.","Rust ExprLinter example: harper-core/src/linting/all_hell_break_loose.rs. It defines `pub struct AllHellBreakLoose { expr: SequenceExpr }` and a Default impl using SequenceExpr::aco("all").t_ws().t_aco("hell").t_ws().then_word_set(&[...]).t_ws().t_aco("out"). It then has `impl ExprLinter` with `type Unit = Chunk`, `match_to_lint` (returns a Lint with LintKind::Eggcorn and Suggestion::replace_with_match_case_str("loose", ..)), `description()` and `expr()`.","Rust tests sit in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in the same file, using `crate::linting::tests::assert_suggestion_result(input, Linter::default(), expected)`.","Rust registry, three places: `mod all_hell_break_loose;` at harper-core/src/linting/mod.rs:11, `use super::all_hell_break_loose::AllHellBreakLoose;` at lint_group.rs:20, and `insert_expr_rule!(AllHellBreakLoose, true);` at lint_group.rs:607. That last list is alphabetical (comment near line 600). Use insert_struct_rule! for non-Expr linters.","Related existing affect/effect confusion: harper-core/src/linting/noun_verb_confusion/effect_affect/{mod.rs,affect_to_effect.rs,effect_to_affect.rs}. Each: `expr main <(flaunt (the|basic|US|his|her|their|its|our|my|your|all|any|)...)` style is too complex; instead use pattern like ColdModalTypo.weir (see /testbed/weir_rules/ColdModalTypo.weir): `expr main <([(flaunt @obj)...]), flaunt>`-style where expr obj is a set [the, rules, laws, law, rule, basic, US, convention, conventions, regulations, regulation, restrictions, speed, limit]. so only flaunt followed by one of these words is flagged (target the first word only). let kind "Usage"? use whichever kind existing rules use for word confusion (e.g. "Eggcorn" or "WordChoice"; check valid kinds), let strategy "MatchCase", message "`Flaunt` means to show off; to openly disregard rules, use `flout`.", tests from: "He flaunted US bankruptcy laws for personal gain.", "It's got a captain who flaunts the rules.", "deranged scientists flaunting the laws of God", "some seem to flaunt the basic rules of punctuation". Add allows "She likes to flaunt her wealth." Then run `cargo test -p harper-core weir` (or the relevant test) and fix until passing. Report result.
